messages:
phish-bot: New user report received from @lina — subject 'Action required: KMS policy update' with attachment 'kms_update.zip' and link https://redwood-kms-update.app. Report submitted via /report-phish.

lina (eng-platform): I clicked nothing but forwarded the raw email to secops. Sender looked like 'billing@redwood-team[.]com' but headers look off. Attachment present.

Samir (secops): Thanks @lina — do not open any attachments. I'm pulling headers and queueing a sandbox detonation now. Can you paste the original raw headers here? Also confirm if you entered any creds or downloaded anything.

lina (eng-platform): pasted headers: ```Received: from mail-45-77-12-9.host by mx.redwood.com; Return-Path: <billing@redwood-team.com>; SPF: fail; DKIM: none; MIME-Version: 1.0; Content-Type: multipart/mixed;``` No creds, did not download exe, only previewed attachment in Gmail but did not open.

phish-bot: Sandbox job #SB-984 queued. Detonation started 2026-03-19T14:05:02Z.

phish-bot: Sandbox result: malicious indicators observed. Payload wrote a binary to /tmp/kms_updater and executed: `./kms_updater --auto`. Observed outgoing POST to https://exfil.example/upload with header 'X-Client: kms-updater/1.2' and attempted metadata calls: `curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` and `aws sts get-caller-identity`. It also attempted to read `~/.aws/credentials`.

Raj (eng-ml): Network analysis shows beaconing to 45.77.12.9 and 198.51.100.42. Reverse DNS for 45.77.12.9 -> cheaphoster-01.proxmails. IPs flagged on ThreatIntel as bulletproof hosting.

Samir (secops): Containment steps we executed: 1) Forced SSO session logout for @lina (IDP revoke) 2) Disabled any OAuth apps recently authorized by @lina — found 'Redwood KMS Updater' OAuth app and revoked tokens 3) Rotated service credentials referenced in /var/logs/kms-deploy — infra-deploy access key deleted and new key issued. Commands used: ```aws iam delete-access-key --user-name infra-deploy --access-key-id AKIAOLD12345```, ```aws iam create-access-key --user-name infra-deploy```.

Samir (secops): Important: we did NOT schedule deletion of primary KMS customer-managed keys. No evidence the key material was exported. Action item: rotate any IAM creds that the process might have used, audit key usage logs for crypto operations in the window.

Taylor (infosec): Adding this to SIEM as incident SEC-2026-1123. Splunk query to find similar activity: ```index=cloud_logs (aws_sts OR aws_iam) earliest=-48h | search "GetCallerIdentity" OR "AssumeRole" | stats count by src_ip, user_agent, aws_account```. Also search proxy logs for redwood-kms-update.app and exfil.example.

Samir (secops): We pulled CloudTrail events for the window 2026-03-19T13:50:00Z -> 2026-03-19T14:10:00Z. Found `GetCallerIdentity` from 198.51.100.42 using role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-deploy-role. We revoked inline session tokens and replaced keys.

Raj (eng-ml): Scanned infra for any run of `/tmp/kms_updater` across fleet: found one additional host where file appeared (host-id: i-0a1b2c3d) — isolated that instance, snapshotting volume for forensics.

Samir (secops): Blocking rules pushed: web-proxy block for redwood-kms-update.app and exfil.example, firewall drop for 45.77.12.9 and 198.51.100.42, YARA rule to detect binary strings 'kms_updater' and 'X-Client: kms-updater'. Also uploaded sample to VT and Malshare.

Natalie (people-ops): We'll coordinate a short digest to Eng: one-paragraph summary + quick dos/don'ts and how to report. Also proposing a 20-min mandatory refresh on phishing basics next week.

Taylor (infosec): Post-incident tasks: 1) update phishing playbook with this IoC set 2) add sandbox indicators to automated quarantine rules 3) reach out to cloud provider abuse to request takedown of exfil domains 4) notify customers if any tenant data access was implicated (none currently).

Samir (secops): For audit trail: added log entries and uploaded timeline to ticket SEC-2026-1123. Evidence artifacts: sandbox logs, network pcap, snapshot of i-0a1b2c3d. Ticket contains recommended remediation steps and owner assignments.

lina (eng-platform): Thanks for quick response. Anything I should do personally?

Samir (secops): You've been through session reset and nothing else. Please rotate any personal AWS keys you may have, enable device MFA if not already, and run the company phishing self-check at the link Natalie will share.

Taylor (infosec): Status: contained. We'll keep this open until full forensics report complete (ETA 48-72h). Will escalate if IOCs appear elsewhere.

Samir (secops): Closing interim incident state as 'contained' — follow-ups in ticket SEC-2026-1123. Reopen if new evidence. :white_check_mark:

phish-bot: Automated note: matched campaign tag 'spearphish-kms-2026'. Adding to org-wide blocklist and to phishing corpus for training sets.

Samir (secops): Logged remediation: blocked domains, rotated creds, isolated host, sandboxed sample. Next: update runbook and coordinate awareness email.

Natalie (people-ops): I'll draft the awareness note and ping @lina for permission to include sanitized screenshots.

Samir (secops): Ticket updated with owners and timelines. Incident thread archived but linked from SEC dashboard.
